title: Fighting AI with AI — Lawrence Jones, Incident
talk_summary: Lawrence Jones of incident.io describes how they debug and improve complex multi-agent AI systems by turning their internal debugging UIs into downloadable file-system snapshots that coding agents (Claude Code/Codex) can grep through, plus a CLI tool so agents can edit large eval YAML files without blowing context. He then runs parallel sub-agent analysis pipelines over batches of production traces to cluster failure modes and drive prompt fixes through an eval red-green runbook.

takeaways.technique: Download debug UI as a file-system snapshot for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of exposing traces/investigations only through a human UI or MCP, they export the entire interaction (all prompts, tool calls, structure) as a self-documenting file tree into a sandbox where a coding agent greps it alongside the codebase.
takeaways.evidence_quote: can we just download all of the UI that we have as a file system? ... we drop that into a sandbox Claude Code

takeaways.technique: CLI wrapper so agents can edit large eval files without context blowup
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a small 'eval tool' CLI exposing list/edit/add/replace operations on eval YAML, so coding agents manipulate test cases via commands instead of loading multi-MB YAML into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we ended up creating a small CLI tool that we call eval tool ... designed to allow agents to leverage our eval suite files

takeaways.technique: Agent runbook for eval red-green prompt fixes
takeaways.what_they_do: A markdown runbook/skill tells the coding agent to first write an eval proving the failure, then modify the prompt until it passes, then re-run the full suite to catch regressions, then consolidate the prompt to avoid bloat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it will create an eval case where it proves that the thing is failed and then it will go modify the prompt so that the eval now passes

takeaways.technique: Parallel sub-agent analysis with cohort clustering
takeaways.what_they_do: A pipeline starts ~25 sub-agents in parallel, each analyzing one investigation and writing results to files, then a clustering stage groups common failure modes into a meta-report with fix recommendations.
All intermediate analysis is written to files inside the downloaded snapshot so a long pipeline can start, stop, and resume rather than losing work on a flaky run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: store all of your analysis in files inside these downloads so that you have like incremental analysis built as you run through it so that you can start and resume

takeaways.technique: Combine trace analysis with codebase to localize the fix
takeaways.what_they_do: Because the downloaded trace sits in the same session as the codebase, the agent can point to the exact prompt/tool in the hierarchy to change and then open a PR, verified by the eval runbook.
